content.title: About
content.content: Plain tortilla chips are crisp, thin slices made from corn tortillas that are fried or baked until golden. They contain no added flavors, making them a versatile base for dips, guacamole, salsa, or as a snack on their own.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortilla chips originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to use leftover corn tortillas.
Traditionally they are made from whole‑grain corn flour, which makes them gluten‑free.
In Mexico similar chips are called “totopos” and are often served with lime and salt.
Tortilla chips are a key component of dishes like nachos and taco salads.
Legend says the first chips were created by accident when a tortilla was over‑fried until crisp.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Corn flour provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with gluten intolerance when made from pure corn flour.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Plain chips contain no added sugars, making them a better choice for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Corn provides carotenoids and phenolic compounds that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some brands are heavily salted, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Crispy chips are calorie‑rich, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to corn products.

items.title: Trans fats in some brands
items.content: If fried in partially hydrogenated oils, chips may contain trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Plain tortilla chips are served with dips (salsa, guacamole, cheese sauce), used in nachos, added to salads for crunch, or enjoyed straight from the bag. They can be reheated briefly in the oven to restore crispness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer them to a tightly sealed bag to maintain crunch and prevent moisture absorption.
